official.description: The NL Scholarship (formerly the Holland Scholarship) is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area who want to do their bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. It amounts to EUR 5,000, received in the first year of studies, and is not a full-tuition scholarship.
official.program_type: Government-funded partial scholarship (Ministry of Education plus Dutch higher education institutions)

verification.notes: Official Study in NL (Nuffic) page read in full on 2026-10-10; confirms EUR 5,000, first-year payment, non-EEA nationality rule, the 'not a full-tuition scholarship' wording, the 2026-2027 opening date of 1 November 2025 and the institution-specific deadline model.

applicant_utility.summary: The NL Scholarship is a one-off EUR 5,000 payment in your first year, awarded by the Dutch institution you apply to rather than by a central body, so the deadline, the eligible programmes and the extra criteria all live on that institution's website. It is explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship, so treat it as a first-year top-up and prove separately that you can fund the rest. Because the participating-institution list is refreshed every year, confirm your programme is on the current list before you build your budget around the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA students admitted to a full-time Dutch bachelor's or master's programme who can cover most costs themselves and want a modest first-year contribution.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the current participating-institutions list and your programme's eligibility for this academic year
Open the institution's own scholarship page and note its closing date; it is the only deadline that counts
Prepare whatever the institution requires (typically a motivation letter and financial plan) alongside your admission application
Confirm you hold no degree from a Dutch institution before applying
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a programme the institution does not include in its NL Scholarship round
Assuming the national 1 November opening date is also the deadline and missing the institution's earlier closing date
Budgeting as if EUR 5,000 covered tuition; the official page states it is not a full-tuition scholarship
Holding a prior degree from a Dutch institution, which disqualifies you outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition (which for non-EEA students is typically far above EUR 5,000), living costs, insurance and travel are all uncovered; the award is a one-year contribution only.
document_audit: Each institution decides its own document set, so never reuse another university's checklist; read your own institution's page before uploading anything
Where the institution asks for a financial plan, it must cover the full duration of the programme, not just year one
alerts: The award was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship; older pages under the old name may quote outdated rules
The participating list changes every academic year, so last year's list is not evidence that your programme still takes part
Nuffic's Integrity Code of Conduct excludes applicants involved in financial misconduct, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission to an eligible programme at a participating institution, indicate or tick the NL Scholarship in that institution's own application, upload what the institution asks for, and wait for the institution's decision.

official.deadline_note: Missing the scholarship deadline means the scholarship application will not be reviewed; reference letters submitted after the deadline are not accepted.
official.status_note: The page publishes the current round with the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 and the 1 December 2026 deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Awarded students receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme based on the Statutory or Institutional rate, according to the registered nationality, AND contribution for the living expenses.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the first year for a TU Delft MSc programme (statutory fee or institutional rate by registered nationality)
Second-year tuition and living allowances conditional on completing at least 48 of 60 ECTS
One of 16 full scholarships each year, two per faculty
eligibility: Excellent international applicant (conditionally) admitted to one of the two-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes (not an International Joint Education Programme)
Amongst the top 10% of graduates in the previous study programme(s), relevant to the master's programme applied for
Complete MSc application submitted before the scholarship deadline
Scholarship holders may not receive any other partial or full scholarship funding in addition
requirements: Complete the MSc application and upload the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029
Upload one reference letter (merge two references into one PDF)
Upload the English language certificate with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline, unless exempt
documents: Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 (PDF published by TU Delft)
One reference letter as a single PDF
English language certificate uploaded with the MSc application before the deadline
selection_criteria: Scholarships are extremely limited and highly competitive, with only the strongest candidates selected
Proof of ranking is not required; the top 10% indication shows the level of competitiveness
Successful students are informed by email by the end of March 2027
coverage: Full tuition fees for the first year (statutory or institutional rate by nationality)
Second-year support conditional on at least 48 of 60 ECTS completed
application_method: Complete the TU Delft MSc application (check the admission requirements)
Upload one reference letter and the English language certificate with the MSc application before 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
official.application_route: Indicate and apply for the scholarship inside the TU Delft MSc application, uploading the form, reference letter and English certificate by 1 December 2026
official.citizenship_residency: Open to excellent international applicants admitted to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme

official.duration: Two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme; second-year allowance conditional on study progress (at least 48 of 60 ECTS)
official.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen; TU Delft offers 16 full scholarships, two per faculty, for its regular MSc programmes, with full tuition fees per year and a contribution towards living expenses.
official.program_type: University excellence scholarship financed by the Justus & Louise van Effen foundation
official.english_requirement: All applicants who wish to be considered for a scholarship must include their English test with their MSc application before the scholarship deadline; exemptions follow the TU Delft MSc admission requirements.

verification.notes: TU Delft scholarships page read in full on 2026-10-10. The brief's URL returned 404; the live official page above carries the full van Effen section. It publishes 16 full scholarships (two per faculty), full tuition fees plus a living-expenses contribution, the 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET) deadline, the 48-of-60 ECTS second-year condition and end-of-March notification, but no euro figure, so all amount fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: Two of these awards exist per faculty, so you are competing against everyone in your faculty rather than the whole university, and the scholarship only exists inside your MSc application: if the MSc file or the reference letter is late, the scholarship file is never reviewed. The award pays full tuition (statutory or institutional rate depending on your nationality) plus a living contribution, and renewal into year two requires at least 48 of 60 ECTS. Note the exclusivity rule: holding any other partial or full scholarship alongside this one is not allowed, so choose between your funding options deliberately.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-decile international applicants to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme who submit a complete admission file in the same round.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the MSc application early; the page warns that missing the scholarship deadline means no review at all
Ask your referee for the letter weeks ahead; late reference letters are not accepted
Check whether you are exempt from the English certificate; if not, book the test so results arrive before 1 December 2026
If you have two referees, merge both letters into a single PDF before uploading
Confirm your programme is a two-year regular MSc and not an International Joint Education Programme
common_rejection_risks: A complete MSc application that arrives after the scholarship deadline, which voids the scholarship file
Applying to an International Joint Education Programme, which is excluded
Already holding a TU Delft bachelor's degree or having started the MSc previously
Counting two separate reference PDFs instead of one merged file
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond tuition and the living contribution, you fund your own relocation, travel, insurance and personal costs; the page publishes no figure for the living contribution, so its real value must be weighed against the TU Delft cost-of-study pages.
document_audit: The reference letter must be a single PDF even when two referees write
The English certificate must be uploaded with the MSc application itself, not emailed afterwards
Exemption from the English test is defined by the MSc admission requirements, not by the scholarship page
alerts: Second-year money depends on finishing at least 48 of 60 ECTS in year one; plan a realistic course load
You cannot combine this award with any other partial or full scholarship
Award decisions come by email by the end of March 2027 and are conditional on meeting all admission criteria
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the TU Delft MSc application, indicate the scholarship, upload the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029, one merged reference letter and the English certificate, then await the faculty decision by email by end of March 2027.
